Appearance:
 Shri Vishal Sharma - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Sudarshan Pandit - Advocate for respondent no.2.

Order 
This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant assailing the impugned award dated 28.05.2024 passed by I Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Biaora, district Rajgarh (M.P.) in Claim Case No.60/2023, whereby the appellant/injured has been awarded an amount of Rs.9,83,987/- along with interest.
2.
Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the only dispute with regard to the income of the deceased is in the instant appeal.

The claims Tribunal has taken income as Rs.6,500/- p.m. whereas as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of Government of Madhya Pradesh the income of an unskilled labour on the date of incident is Rs.9,325/-.

entities.text: Labour Department of Government of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On this submission prays for enhancement of the award amount.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8931 2 MA-7798-2024 3.

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that the income has been properly assessed by the Claims Tribunal and needs no enhancement and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

The Apex Court in the case of Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. Vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093 has held that where the income of the deceased is taken on guess work, circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act should be resorted to.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of the aforesaid, on the date of accident i.e. on 08.03.2023 income of the deceased is to be taken as Rs.9,325/- considering him as 'Unskilled Labour', whereas the learned Claims Tribunal has taken the income as Rs.6,500/- only.

Accordingly, the just and proper compensation comes as under:-
Rs.Rs.9,325/- +Rs.932 (10% FP) x 12 =Rs.1,23,084/- Permanent per annum x 11(
Multiplier) x 75% PD = Disablement Rs.10,15,443/-
Loss of income during treatment Rs.9,325 x 3 =Rs.27,975/-
Physical Pain and Rs.50,000/-
 mental agony  Medicines and  treatment Rs.1,51,737-  expenses  Special diet Rs.13,500/-
 Transportation Rs.5,000/-
 Attendant charges Rs.13,500/-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8931 3 MA-7798-2024 Loss of amenities and enjoyment of Rs.1,00,000/-

life Total: Rs.13,77,155/-
MACT Award: Rs.9,83,987/-
Enhanced Amount Rs.3,93,168/-
7.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.13,77,155/- as against the award of the Tribunal o f Rs.9,83,987/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.3,93,168/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the same rate as has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
